full_text_en:
Wang Aiying v. Li Baosheng — Compulsory Execution Dispute over Homestead Plot

Plaintiff: Wang Aiying, female, 37 years old, a native of Huaxian County, Henan Province, accountant at the Service Society of the 86364 Unit of the People's Liberation Army, residing at No. 74 Wenhuali, Erqi District, Zhengzhou.

Defendant: Li Baosheng, male, 54 years old, a native of Lingchuan County, Shanxi Province, Deputy Secretary of the Party Branch and Director of Zhengzhou Noodle Factory, residing at No. 73 Wenhuali, Erqi District, Zhengzhou.

The plaintiff, Wang Aiying, and the defendant, Li Baosheng, were next-door neighbors. In May 1980, Wang Aiying, with the approval of the Construction Section of Erqi District, Zhengzhou, renovated six rooms on the second floor of the north house on the original foundation of her own house at No. 74 Wenhuali, with its rear wall facing Li Baosheng's courtyard. Li Baosheng claimed that there were women in his family, which would cause inconvenience, and refused to allow Wang Aiying to open windows on the rear wall. After mediation by the neighborhood committee and the district Construction Section, the two parties reached an agreement: Wang Aiying would leave a small window on the lower east room of the rear wall; when Li Baosheng built a new house, his south wall would be constructed directly against the rear wall of Wang Aiying's house on the original foundation, and no windows would be allowed on the rear wall. In June 1980, Li Baosheng applied for building approval, obtained a permit, but commenced construction without line verification or positioning by the construction department, violating the permit's requirement of "commence construction after line verification." Furthermore, without consulting Wang Aiying, Li Baosheng changed the originally agreed south house to a west house, dug the foundation directly against Wang Aiying's rear wall, causing overlapping foundations and threatening the safety of Wang Aiying's house. Wang Aiying stopped his construction, but Li ignored her. The Erqi District Construction Section repeatedly informed him to stop work, but he still refused, and ultimately revoked his building permit, instructing him to await further action. Li Baosheng continued construction. Wang Aiying's husband, Cheng Xueling, intervened, and Li Baosheng assaulted and injured him. Consequently, on July 15, 1980, Wang Aiying filed a lawsuit with the Erqi District People's Court of Zhengzhou.

After accepting the case, the Erqi District People's Court, on the basis of ascertaining the facts, notified the defendant, Li Baosheng, to suspend construction pending resolution. Li Baosheng ignored the court's notice, rushed to complete the house, and even placed his eaves on top of Wang Aiying's roof eaves, causing excessive pressure on the foundation of Wang Aiying's building, resulting in wall cracks and water leakage. Accordingly, the Erqi District People's Court held a public trial of the case. The trial found that the defendant, Li Baosheng, had built the house without complying with the building permit's requirement of "commence construction after line verification" and, after the dispute arose, refused to accept the Construction Section's handling opinions and rushed to complete construction, constituting an act of illegal construction. The Construction Section and the plaintiff had repeatedly stopped these illegal acts, but the defendant ignored them, incorporated the plaintiff's eaves into his own eaves, and assaulted and injured the plaintiff's husband, Cheng Xueling, thereby infringing on the rights and personal integrity of others. On November 25, 1980, in accordance with national policies, the court ruled that the defendant, Li Baosheng, must demolish the south gable wall of the illegally constructed west house, move it 50 centimeters north, and be responsible for repairing the wall cracks in the plaintiff's house and resolving the water leakage problem; and compensate Cheng Xueling for medical expenses of 16.14 yuan incurred from his assault and hospitalization.

Li Baosheng, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court, arguing that his construction had a permit and was not illegal, and that building against Wang Aiying's rear wall was in execution of the agreement between the parties.

After accepting the appeal, the Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court conducted a comprehensive review of the facts found and policies applied by the first-instance court. It held that the facts found in the original judgment were clear, the evidence was conclusive, and the procedure was lawful. As to the appellant's claim that "the construction had a permit and was not illegal," investigation revealed that although Li Baosheng's construction was approved by the district Construction Section and a permit was issued, the permit explicitly stated "commence construction after line verification," but Li Baosheng started construction arbitrarily without line verification by the district Construction Section. Thereafter, the plaintiff, the district Construction Section, and the first-instance court repeatedly informed Li Baosheng to cease construction pending resolution. Not only did Li refuse to comply, but he also unilaterally altered the positions of the south house room and staircase as specified in the permit, and assaulted the parties involved. This was clearly an act of illegal construction and infringement of personal rights. As to the appellant's claim that building against Wang Aiying's rear wall was "execution of the agreement between the parties," investigation revealed that the original agreement stated that "when Li Baosheng builds a house, the south wall shall be constructed directly against the rear wall of Wang Aiying's house from the east gable to the west gable on the original foundation," but the original agreement referred to Li Baosheng building a south house. The defendant privately changed it to a west house without prior consultation with Wang Aiying, and placed the foundation of his house on top of Wang Aiying's foundation, endangering the safety of Wang Aiying's house. This was clearly the defendant's own violation of the original agreement.

Accordingly, on September 19, 1981, the Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered a final judgment: appeal dismissed, and the original judgment affirmed.

Li Baosheng, dissatisfied with the final judgment of the Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court, petitioned the Henan High People's Court.

After review, the Henan High People's Court issued a notice on July 13, 1982, stating that the petition was unfounded and rejected.

Li Baosheng, dissatisfied with the notice of rejection by the Henan High People's Court and refusing to comply with the judgments of the first and second instance courts, petitioned the Supreme People's Court.

After sending personnel to the scene for inspection and investigation, the Supreme People's Court concluded that Li Baosheng's construction had infringed Wang Aiying's lawful rights and interests, and that the Henan High People's Court's notice rejecting his petition was correct. On March 28, 1983, in accordance with Article 158, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), the Supreme People's Court notified Li Baosheng that his petition was rejected.

To uphold the dignity of the law and protect the plaintiff's lawful rights and interests, on July 3, 1983, the Erqi District People's Court, in accordance with Article 177 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), issued a public notice signed by the court president, ordering Li Baosheng to comply with the court's judgment within ten days; if he failed to do so by the deadline, compulsory execution measures would be taken according to law.

Upon expiration of the public notice period, Li Baosheng did not comply with the court's judgment. On July 13, the Erqi District People's Court carried out compulsory execution according to law. In accordance with Article 177, paragraph 3 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), the court invited representatives from the local police station, subdistrict office, neighborhood committee, district Construction Section, and the defendant's work unit to be present at the scene. The enforcement officers organized engineering technicians and workers to demolish the gable wall that the defendant had already built and moved it 50 centimeters north. The execution was completed on July 30. The total cost of labor and materials for the compulsory execution was 765.85 yuan, all borne by Li Baosheng (Li Baosheng paid the full amount to the Erqi District People's Court).

On May 23, 1986, the 259th meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with Article 11, paragraph 1 of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, summarized trial experience and held that parties must execute legally effective judgments, rulings, and mediation agreements. In the case of Li Baosheng v. Wang Aiying dispute over homestead plot, after the court's judgment became legally effective, Li Baosheng could file a petition if dissatisfied with the judgment, but could not suspend execution of the judgment. Li Baosheng's refusal to execute the court's judgment during the petition period violated legal provisions. Under these circumstances, the Erqi District People's Court, in order to uphold the seriousness of the law and protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties, took compulsory measures to execute the judgment, reflecting the spirit of strict law enforcement.
